summary: Backend-only verification of iter413ck GSC OAuth redirect URI fix. The backend now derives the OAuth callback URI from the inbound request's x-forwarded-host/proto headers (with env var override still honored), and binds the resolved URI to the CSRF state token so the token-exchange call uses the exact URI Google saw. All 5 contract tests pass + 4 additional verification tests pass + iter351 GSC regression still passes (15/15 total).
critical_code_review_comments: gsc_admin.py is at ~530 lines — still under the 700-line split threshold, fine for now but consider extracting the indexation-summary / snapshots-trend handlers into a separate module if more endpoints are added.

_resolve_redirect_uri correctly defends against comma-separated x-forwarded-host header values (`.split(',')[0].strip()`) — good. Equally important: the function uses `request.url.scheme` fallback for scheme, which behind Kubernetes ingress is `http` — verified via the live test that x-forwarded-proto is being honored, so the production redirect URI emerges as `https://...` correctly.

Security note: anyone who can spoof the x-forwarded-host header on a public endpoint could trick the backend into emitting an attacker-controlled redirect_uri at /admin/gsc/status. Risk is bounded because (a) /status is admin-auth gated, (b) /oauth-start is admin-auth gated, and (c) Google itself only honors redirect URIs whitelisted in the Cloud Console. So the worst an attacker could do is force a `redirect_uri_mismatch` rejection — denial of OAuth, not exfiltration. Acceptable.

_oauth_state is in-memory — if the backend is ever scaled horizontally, the state set on pod A won't be visible to pod B on callback, causing 'Invalid or expired state' errors intermittently. Since this is a single-admin flow taking <30s, it's fine today, but worth a TODO comment if Crafters Market ever runs multi-pod.
